Find all solutions to \( 2\sin\theta-1=0 \) on \( [0,2\pi) \). \[ \sin\theta=\tfrac{1}{2} \implies \theta=\tfrac{\pi}{6} \text{ or } \theta=\tfrac{5\pi}{6}. \]

caption.en: The triangle's known sides/angle and the computed third side

body.en: Law of Sines: \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}\). Law of Cosines: \(c^2 = a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C\). Key identities: \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\); \(\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\); \(\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta\).

A triangle has sides \(a=7, b=10\) and included angle \(C=60°\). Find side \(c\).

\(c^2 = 49 + 100 - 2(7)(10)\cos 60° = 149 - 70 = 79\). \(c = \sqrt{79} \approx 8.89\).

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Trigonometry & Angle Measures

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Calculator Mode: ACT questions mix degrees (e.g. \(120°\)) and radians (e.g. \(2\pi/3\)). Check your calculator mode before every trig calculation! If you get unexpected decimals for standard values, check the mode first.
  • Signs by Quadrant (ASTC): In Quadrant II, sine is positive but cosine and tangent are negative. In Quadrant III, tangent is positive but sine and cosine are negative. In Quadrant IV, cosine is positive but sine and tangent are negative.
  • The Ambiguous Case (SSA): When using the Law of Sines with two sides and an opposite angle (SSA), always check whether the supplementary angle \(180° - B\) can form a valid second triangle (sum of angles < 180°).
  • Double-Angle Cosine Forms: Remember the three equivalent forms: \(\cos(2\theta) = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\). Choosing the form matching the other terms simplifies quadratic trig equations immediately.

question.en: Solve the quadratic trigonometric equation \(2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0\) for all solutions \(\theta \in [0, 2\pi)\).

solution.en:
Factoring: Factor as a quadratic in \(\sin\theta\): \[ (2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0. \]

Case 1: \(2\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\), sine is positive in Quadrants I and II with reference angle \(\pi/6\): \[ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\quad \theta = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}. \]

Case 2: \(\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = 1\). In \([0, 2\pi)\), sine equals 1 at \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

Complete solution set: \(\left\{ \dfrac{\pi}{6},\, \dfrac{\pi}{2},\, \dfrac{5\pi}{6} \right\}\).
